record.paper_title: Mini-Proceedings ECT* Workshop: Hadronic Atoms and Kaonic Nuclei
record.original_question: For reported structures in Λp, ppπ−, and related invariant-mass spectra from experiments such as E549, FINUDA, OBELIX, FOPI, and older K−d bubble-chamber observations, are the peaks evidence for Bound Kaonic Systems, or can they instead be explained by conventional mechanisms such as threshold cusp effects, two-nucleon absorption, ΣN conversion, or other final-state effects?

evidence.quote: It might be useful to point out at possible similarities of possible Bound Kaonic Systems (BKS) observations reported at this Workshop and performed in different experimental environments, as a start for a thorough understanding of a few disagreements among some of them.
For this structure both the interpretation of BKS or of threshold effect can in principle be suggested.

the signal was indicated to be due to a cusp effect related to the opening of the Σ0nπ− channel, rather than to a new resonance. Also in this case an alternative interpretation of the recently observed signal can be suggested.

artifact.status_search_result: The interpretation of reported Λp and ppπ⁻ peaks as bound kaonic systems versus conventional final-state effects (cusps, two-nucleon absorption, ΣN conversion) remains unresolved. Critical analyses (e.g., arXiv:0801.4504, arXiv:nucl-th/0609070) have argued against the BKS interpretation of several signals, while FINUDA and OBELIX collaborations maintain BKS interpretations. Subsequent J-PARC E15/E80 measurements have observed a K⁻pp-like structure but its nature is still debated, so the unified interpretation question is open.

status_evidence.title: Critical review of [K- ppn] bound states
status_evidence.snippet: Critical review of bound kaonic states questioning the BKS interpretation of FINUDA and similar signals.
status_evidence.claim: Several reported peaks have been argued to admit conventional explanations rather than BKS.

status_evidence.title: Recent results on K− absorption at rest by few nucleons and the bound kaonic nuclear state puzzle
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the puzzle of bound kaonic nuclear states in light of K- absorption data.
status_evidence.claim: The status of bound kaonic nuclear states from K- absorption is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: A critical analysis on deeply bound kaonic states in nuclei and the KEK experiment
status_evidence.snippet: Critical analysis arguing alternative mechanisms for observed peaks.
status_evidence.claim: Conventional mechanisms can plausibly account for some signals attributed to BKS.
